subject: Defining acceptance tests & exit gates for NovaCare pilot
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@novacare.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Lim <aaron.lim@novacare.io>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot acceptance tests — draft questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profile and the redaction examples. Before we lock dates for the 4-week pilot, procurement wanted a clearer list of acceptance tests and what counts as a pass. Can you send a short, prioritized list of acceptance criteria with concrete checks and minimal required evidence?

Two quick asks from our side:
- Does the pilot include per-request logging for audit (we need timestamp + model version)
- If performance regresses >20% on average latency, what is the rollback/mitigation path?

Would appreciate a one-page matrix we can share with procurement.

Best,
Emily
VP Product, NovaCare

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@novacare.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance tests — draft questions

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear asks. I put together an initial matrix attached (novacare_acceptance_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a short sample prompt set. High-level answers here and in the sheet: 

1) Audit logs: yes — hosted pilot includes per-request metadata (timestamp, model id, token count, request id). We'll provide a read-only S3 export for the 4-week window.

2) Performance regression policy: we classify regressions as degraded (10-20%) and critical (>20%). For degraded, we'll throttle batch size and enable prefix caching which typically recovers within one hour; for critical we failover to the pinned cheaper variant and open an incident. We document rollback steps in the "Operational Failover" column in the sheet.

Next steps I propose:
- You review the attached matrix and highlight the top 3 must-have acceptance tests for procurement.
- We align on evidence formats (CSV logs, sample responses, smoke runbook).
- Sign mutual action plan addendum in DocuSign once agreed.

Looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Ben (reliability) to confirm evidence formats and how we'll run the smoke tests.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@novacare.io>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance tests — draft questions

Emily — attaching the sample prompt set (sample_prompt_set.txt) and a short smoke test runbook excerpt inside the workbook. A few clarifying notes on evidence we typically provide: 

- For functional acceptance (accuracy/concordance): 50 labeled examples from your domain, we return model outputs + manual pass/fail labels and an automated concordance score. Pass threshold: >= 85% concordance on the labeled set.

- For latency SLO: 95th percentile < 350ms for 1-2 token responses and < 650ms for 100-token responses under designated load.

- For reliability: <1% error rate (HTTP 5xx) across the pilot.

If these look reasonable, Kimberly — can you add the exact artifact names NovaCare should expect us to drop into the shared Drive and the timeline for when each artifact will be available during the 4-week pilot?

-Marissa
Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Aaron Lim <aaron.lim@novacare.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@novacare.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance tests — draft questions

Thanks — quick procurement note: they want the acceptance criteria mapped to contract milestones (payment and trial extension triggers). For example:

- Milestone 1 (Week 1): Connectivity + baseline smoke test passed (artifact: connectivity_report.csv) => 25% invoice release.
- Milestone 2 (End Week 2): Functional concordance >= 85% on labeled set (artifact: concordance_report.csv) => 25% invoice release.
- Milestone 3 (End Week 4): Final report + recommendations and go/no-go signoff => remaining invoice.

Question: if concordance falls 5-10% below threshold, is there a remediation sprint included in the pilot window or does that trigger an extension (and cost) discussion?

-Aaron
Director, Procurement
NovaCare

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lim <aaron.lim@novacare.io>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 15:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance tests — draft questions

Aaron/Emily — quick reply with the pragmatic approach we took on other pilots:

- If concordance is within 5-10% below threshold at the Week 2 check, we include a one-week remediation sprint (no additional pilot fee) to tune prompts/labels and run another evaluation. That sprint includes up to two optimization cycles (prompt adjustments + model variant changes).
- If after remediation concordance remains >10% below threshold, either party can choose not to proceed; procurement milestones tied to the second payment are paused until mutual signoff.

Deliverables & timing (we'll push artifacts to the shared Drive at these times):
- End of Week 0 (pre-pilot): connectivity_report.csv, baseline_latency.csv
- End of Week 2: concordance_report.csv, interim-smoke-log.csv
- End of Week 4: final_report.pdf, incident-log.csv

I'll update the acceptance matrix to explicitly show the remediation lane and milestone gating. Once you confirm the three milestones and remediation flow, Kim will attach the mutual action plan addendum and we'll start DocuSign.

-Ben
Reliability Eng & Pilot Ops
Redwood Inference
